\chapter{Taking On the Work}
\label{ch:ml-taking-on-the-work}
\hlchaptermodality{551}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say to entrust, to take on, to attain, to put in work and to toil.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 551: I can say to entrust, to take on, to attain, to put in work and to toil.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഏൽപ്പിക്കുക} (ēlppikkuka)}{ഏൽപ്പിക്കുക (ēlppikkuka)}]{\ml{ഏൽപ്പിക്കുക} (ēlppikkuka) — to entrust; to hand over (a task)}

\label{lesson:ML-C551-elppikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to consult, then the Malayalam for an interval.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഏൽപ്പിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഏൽപ്പിക്കുക}} — \emph{ēlppikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to entrust; to hand over (a task)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മാനേജർ} \ml{പുതിയ} \ml{ജോലി} \ml{എന്നെ} \ml{ഏൽപ്പിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mānējar putiya jōli enne ēlppiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager entrusted the new work to me.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഏൽപ്പിച്ചു}, \emph{ēlppiccu}.

The person entrusted takes -\ml{എ}; the task stays plain.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഏൽപ്പിക്കുക}} (\emph{ēlppikkuka}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 905 lists \ml{ഏൽക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to receive, to take in charge\textquotedblright{}, and its causative, to make someone take it on (DEDR 905).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēlppikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēlppikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mānējar putiya jōli enne ēlppiccu.} — The manager entrusted the new work to me.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to consult, then the Malayalam for an interval, then say \emph{ēlppikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഏൽപ്പിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To entrust; to hand over (a task)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഏറ്റെടുക്കുക} (ēṟṟeṭukkuka)}{ഏറ്റെടുക്കുക (ēṟṟeṭukkuka)}]{\ml{ഏറ്റെടുക്കുക} (ēṟṟeṭukkuka) — to take on; to undertake}

\label{lesson:ML-C551-erretukkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for an interval, then the Malayalam for to entrust.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഏറ്റെടുക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഏറ്റെടുക്കുക}} — \emph{ēṟṟeṭukkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to take on; to undertake\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പരിപാടിയുടെ} \ml{ചുമതല} \ml{അവൾ} \ml{ഏറ്റെടുത്തു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{paripāṭiyuṭe cumatala avaḷ ēṟṟeṭuttu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She took charge of the programme.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഏറ്റെടുത്തു}, \emph{ēṟṟeṭuttu}.

\ml{ഏറ്റ്}, having received, + \ml{എടുക്കുക}, to take.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഏറ്റെടുക്കുക}} (\emph{ēṟṟeṭukkuka}) is native Dravidian, a compound of \ml{ഏൽക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to receive, to take in charge\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 905), and \ml{എടുക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to take up, to undertake\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 851).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēṟṟeṭukkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēṟṟeṭukkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paripāṭiyuṭe cumatala avaḷ ēṟṟeṭuttu.} — She took charge of the programme.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for an interval, then the Malayalam for to entrust, then say \emph{ēṟṟeṭukkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കൈവരിക്കുക} (kaivarikkuka)}{കൈവരിക്കുക (kaivarikkuka)}]{\ml{കൈവരിക്കുക} (kaivarikkuka) — to attain; to achieve}

\label{lesson:ML-C551-kaivarikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to entrust, then the Malayalam for to take on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കൈവരിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{കൈവരിക്കുക}} — \emph{kaivarikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to attain; to achieve\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{കഠിനാധ്വാനത്തിലൂടെ} \ml{അവൻ} \ml{വിജയം} \ml{കൈവരിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kaṭhinādhvānattilūṭe avan vijayaṁ kaivariccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He achieved success through hard work.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{കൈവരിച്ചു}, \emph{kaivariccu}.

Formal, said of success and goals.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കൈവരിക്കുക}} (\emph{kaivarikkuka}) holds \ml{കൈ}, \textquotedblleft{}hand\textquotedblright{}, which is native (DEDR 2023); the origin of the second part is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaivarikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭhinādhvānattilūṭe avan vijayaṁ kaivariccu.} — He achieved success through hard work.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to entrust, then the Malayalam for to take on, then say \emph{kaivarikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{പണിയെടുക്കുക} (paṇiyeṭukkuka)}{പണിയെടുക്കുക (paṇiyeṭukkuka)}]{\ml{പണിയെടുക്കുക} (paṇiyeṭukkuka) — to put in work; to labour}

\label{lesson:ML-C551-paniyetukkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to take on, then the Malayalam for to attain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പണിയെടുക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{പണിയെടുക്കുക}} — \emph{paṇiyeṭukkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to put in work; to labour\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അച്ഛൻ} \ml{രാവിലെ} \ml{മുതൽ} \ml{പറമ്പിൽ} \ml{പണിയെടുത്തു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{acchan rāvile mutal paṟampil paṇiyeṭuttu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Father worked in the yard from the morning on.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{പണിയെടുത്തു}, \emph{paṇiyeṭuttu}.

\ml{പണി} work + \ml{എടുക്കുക} to take: plain spoken Malayalam for hard work.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{പണിയെടുക്കുക}} (\emph{paṇiyeṭukkuka}) is native Dravidian, a compound of \ml{പണി}, \textquotedblleft{}work, labour\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3884), and \ml{എടുക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to take up\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 851).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṇiyeṭukkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{acchan rāvile mutal paṟampil paṇiyeṭuttu.} — Father worked in the yard from the morning on.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to take on, then the Malayalam for to attain, then say \emph{paṇiyeṭukkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{അധ്വാനിക്കുക} (adhvānikkuka)}{അധ്വാനിക്കുക (adhvānikkuka)}]{\ml{അധ്വാനിക്കുക} (adhvānikkuka) — to toil; to labour}

\label{lesson:ML-C551-adhvanikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to attain, then the Malayalam for to put in work.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{അധ്വാനിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{അധ്വാനിക്കുക}} — \emph{adhvānikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to toil; to labour\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{കുടുംബത്തിന്} \ml{വേണ്ടി} \ml{അച്ഛൻ} \ml{രാവും} \ml{പകലും} \ml{അധ്വാനിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kuṭumbattinŭ vēṇṭi acchan rāvuṁ pakaluṁ adhvāniccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Father toiled day and night for the family.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{അധ്വാനിച്ചു}, \emph{adhvāniccu}.

The noun is \ml{അധ്വാനം}, toil; \ml{കഠിനാധ്വാനി} holds it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{അധ്വാനിക്കുക}} (\emph{adhvānikkuka}) is built on \ml{അധ്വാനം}, \textquotedblleft{}toil\textquotedblright{}, with the Malayalam verb ending -\ml{ിക്കുക}; where \ml{അധ്വാനം} itself comes from is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adhvānikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuṭumbattinŭ vēṇṭi acchan rāvuṁ pakaluṁ adhvāniccu.} — Father toiled day and night for the family.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to attain, then the Malayalam for to put in work, then say \emph{adhvānikkuka} again
\end{itemize}
